views.name: order_revenue

columns.name: ordered_at
columns.description: When the order was placed (timestamptz, UTC).

columns.name: status
columns.description: placed, shipped, delivered or returned (cancelled orders are excluded).

columns.name: region_code
columns.description: NA, EU, UK, APAC or LATAM.

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Attributed campaign (campaigns.id); NULL for orders without a campaign.

columns.name: gross_revenue_usd
columns.description: Items minus discounts, in USD, before refunds.

columns.name: refund_usd
columns.description: Refunds of this order, in USD.

views.description: One row per valid order (not cancelled, not soft-deleted, not a test account) with its revenue in USD. Use it for revenue, order counts and average order value by date, region, country, channel, campaign or segment.
views.sql:
SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.customer_id, o.ordered_at, CAST(o.ordered_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS DATE) AS order_date,
       o.status, rg.code AS region_code, rg.name AS region_name, o.country_code, o.currency_code,
       o.channel_id, ch.name AS channel_name, o.campaign_id, c.segment AS customer_segment, li.units,
       li.items_amount * fx.usd_per_unit AS gross_revenue_usd,
       COALESCE(rf.refund_amount, 0) * fx.usd_per_unit AS refund_usd,
       (li.items_amount - COALESCE(rf.refund_amount, 0)) * fx.usd_per_unit AS net_revenue_usd
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN regions rg ON rg.id = o.region_id
JOIN marketing_channels ch ON ch.id = o.channel_id
JOIN fx_rates fx ON fx.currency_code = o.currency_code AND fx.rate_date = CAST(o.ordered_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS DATE)
JOIN (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price - discount_amount) AS items_amount, SUM(quantity) AS units
      FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) li ON li.order_id = o.id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) AS refund_amount FROM refunds GROUP BY order_id) rf ON rf.order_id = o.id
WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL AND NOT c.is_test_account

views.name: order_line_revenue

columns.name: ordered_at
columns.description: When the order was placed (timestamptz, UTC).

columns.name: region_code
columns.description: NA, EU, UK, APAC or LATAM.

columns.name: parent_category_name
columns.description: Top-level category - Lighting, Smart Home or Accessories.

columns.name: gross_revenue_usd
columns.description: Line amount minus discount, in USD.

columns.name: refund_usd
columns.description: Refunds of this line, in USD.

columns.name: cost_usd
columns.description: Unit cost times quantity, in USD.

views.description: One row per order line of a valid order, with product, category and revenue in USD. Use it for product and category questions (units sold, product revenue, product refunds, margin). Goodwill refunds that are not tied to a product are not included here, so product-level net revenue sums to slightly more than order_revenue.
views.sql:
SELECT oi.id AS order_item_id, o.id AS order_id, o.customer_id, o.ordered_at,
       CAST(o.ordered_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS DATE) AS order_date, rg.code AS region_code, o.country_code,
       o.channel_id, o.campaign_id, p.id AS product_id, p.name AS product_name, cat.id AS category_id,
       cat.name AS category_name, parent.name AS parent_category_name, oi.quantity AS units,
       (oi.quantity * oi.unit_price - oi.discount_amount) * fx.usd_per_unit AS gross_revenue_usd,
       COALESCE(rf.amount, 0) * fx.usd_per_unit AS refund_usd,
       (oi.quantity * oi.unit_price - oi.discount_amount - COALESCE(rf.amount, 0)) * fx.usd_per_unit AS net_revenue_usd,
       oi.quantity * p.unit_cost_usd AS cost_usd
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN regions rg ON rg.id = o.region_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN categories cat ON cat.id = p.category_id
LEFT JOIN categories parent ON parent.id = cat.parent_id
JOIN fx_rates fx ON fx.currency_code = o.currency_code AND fx.rate_date = CAST(o.ordered_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS DATE)
LEFT JOIN (SELECT order_item_id, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM refunds WHERE order_item_id IS NOT NULL
           GROUP BY order_item_id) rf ON rf.order_item_id = oi.id
WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND o.deleted_at IS NULL AND NOT c.is_test_account

views.name: customer_profile

columns.name: region_code
columns.description: NA, EU, UK, APAC or LATAM.

columns.name: acquisition_channel
columns.description: Channel that acquired the customer, or NULL when unknown.

columns.name: marketing_opt_in
columns.description: Whether the customer accepts marketing email.

columns.name: first_order_at
columns.description: First valid order (NULL if the customer never ordered).

views.description: One row per real customer (soft-deleted customers and test accounts excluded) with region, segment, signup and first and last valid order. Use it for customer counts, new customers, cohorts and retention.
views.sql:
SELECT c.id AS customer_id, c.name AS customer_name, c.city, c.country_code, rg.code AS region_code, c.segment,
       c.signup_at, CAST(c.signup_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS DATE) AS signup_date, ch.name AS acquisition_channel,
       c.marketing_opt_in, fo.first_order_at, fo.last_order_at, COALESCE(fo.order_count, 0) AS order_count
FROM customers c
JOIN regions rg ON rg.id = c.region_id
LEFT JOIN marketing_channels ch ON ch.id = c.acquisition_channel_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT customer_id, MIN(ordered_at) AS first_order_at, MAX(ordered_at) AS last_order_at,
                  COUNT(*) AS order_count
           FROM orders WHERE status <> 'cancelled' AND deleted_at IS NULL GROUP BY customer_id) fo
       ON fo.customer_id = c.id
WHERE c.deleted_at IS NULL AND NOT c.is_test_account

views.name: subscription_revenue

columns.name: region_code
columns.description: NA, EU, UK, APAC or LATAM.

columns.name: plan_name
columns.description: Care Basic, Care Plus or Care Pro.

views.description: One row per paid Lumora Care invoice with the plan and the amount in USD (converted on the invoice's period start date). Use it for subscription revenue by month, plan or region. Test accounts are excluded.
views.sql:
SELECT i.id AS invoice_id, i.subscription_id, s.customer_id, rg.code AS region_code, p.id AS plan_id,
       p.name AS plan_name, p.billing_period, i.issued_at, i.period_start, i.period_end,
       i.amount * fx.usd_per_unit AS amount_usd
FROM invoices i
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.id = i.subscription_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = s.customer_id
JOIN plans p ON p.id = s.plan_id
JOIN regions rg ON rg.id = s.region_id
JOIN fx_rates fx ON fx.currency_code = i.currency_code AND fx.rate_date = i.period_start
WHERE i.status = 'paid' AND NOT c.is_test_account
